topic: Semaglutide and tirzepatide for obesity: weight-loss efficacy in clinical trials and main safety concerns

key_points.point: In the Wegovy label's 68-week obesity trial (STEP 1 per published literature; label calls it Study 2), semaglutide 2.4 mg gave -14.9% vs -2.4% placebo; 83.5% lost at least 5% and 47.9% at least 15%.

atoms.fact: In the Wegovy label's 68-week obesity trial (STEP 1 in published literature; the label calls it Study 2), semaglutide 2.4 mg gave -14.9% weight change versus -2.4% with placebo.
In the Wegovy label's 68-week obesity trial (STEP 1 in published literature; the label calls it Study 2), 83.5% of semaglutide 2.4 mg patients lost at least 5% of body weight.
In the Wegovy label's 68-week obesity trial (STEP 1 in published literature; the label calls it Study 2), 47.9% of semaglutide 2.4 mg patients lost at least 15% of body weight.

key_points.point: SURMOUNT-1 (2,539 adults without diabetes, 72 weeks): tirzepatide 5/10/15 mg gave about -15% / -20% / -21% mean weight change versus about -3% on placebo (label: -15.0/-19.5/-20.9 vs -3.1; efficacy estimand: -16.0/-21.4/-22.5 vs -2.4); roughly 85-96% lost at least 5%. Either set of figures counts.

atoms.fact: SURMOUNT-1 was a 72-week trial in 2,539 adults without diabetes.

In SURMOUNT-1, tirzepatide 5/10/15 mg gave about -15% / -20% / -21% mean weight change versus about -3% on placebo (label: -15.0/-19.5/-20.9 vs -3.1; efficacy estimand: -16.0/-21.4/-22.5 vs -2.4); either set of figures counts.
In SURMOUNT-1, roughly 85-96% of tirzepatide patients lost at least 5% of body weight.

key_points.point: Head-to-head SURMOUNT-5 (751 adults with obesity, no diabetes, 72 weeks): tirzepatide produced 20.2% mean weight loss versus 13.7% with semaglutide, with similar GI-dominated safety profiles.

atoms.fact: In the head-to-head SURMOUNT-5 trial (751 adults with obesity, no diabetes, 72 weeks), tirzepatide produced 20.2% mean weight loss versus 13.7% with semaglutide.
In SURMOUNT-5, tirzepatide and semaglutide had similar, GI-dominated safety profiles.

key_points.point: Gastrointestinal events are the most common adverse reactions: with semaglutide 2.4 mg nausea 44% (placebo 16%), diarrhea 30%, vomiting 24%, constipation 24%; mostly during dose escalation.

atoms.fact: Gastrointestinal events are the most common adverse reactions of semaglutide and tirzepatide obesity treatment.
With semaglutide 2.4 mg, nausea occurs in 44% versus 16% with placebo.
With semaglutide 2.4 mg, diarrhea occurs in 30%.
With semaglutide 2.4 mg, vomiting occurs in 24% and constipation in 24%.
Gastrointestinal adverse reactions to semaglutide 2.4 mg occur mostly during dose escalation.

key_points.point: Discontinuation due to adverse reactions with tirzepatide was about 5-7% across doses versus about 3% on placebo (label pooled: 4.8% / 6.3% / 6.7% vs 3.4%).

atoms.fact: Discontinuation due to adverse reactions with tirzepatide was about 5-7% across doses versus about 3% on placebo (label pooled: 4.8% / 6.3% / 6.7% vs 3.4%).

key_points.point: Both Wegovy and Zepbound carry a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors (seen in rodents; human relevance unknown) and are contraindicated with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.

atoms.fact: Both Wegovy and Zepbound carry a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors (seen in rodents; human relevance unknown).
Both Wegovy and Zepbound are contraindicated with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.

key_points.point: Beyond GI effects, label warnings include acute pancreatitis, acute gallbladder disease and acute kidney injury from volume depletion (also hypoglycemia, diabetic retinopathy complications in type 2 diabetes, severe GI adverse reactions and pulmonary aspiration under anesthesia); naming pancreatitis, gallbladder disease and one other warning counts.

atoms.fact: Beyond GI effects, the Wegovy/Zepbound label warnings include acute pancreatitis.
Beyond GI effects, the Wegovy/Zepbound label warnings include acute gallbladder disease.

The Wegovy/Zepbound label warnings include at least one further warning besides pancreatitis and gallbladder disease: acute kidney injury from volume depletion, hypoglycemia, diabetic retinopathy complications in type 2 diabetes, severe GI adverse reactions, or pulmonary aspiration under anesthesia (naming any one of these counts).

key_points.point: Stopping treatment leads to substantial weight regain: in SURMOUNT-4, patients switched to placebo regained about 14% of body weight between weeks 36 and 88, while those continuing tirzepatide lost a further 5.5%.

atoms.fact: Stopping semaglutide or tirzepatide obesity treatment leads to substantial weight regain.
In SURMOUNT-4, patients switched to placebo regained about 14% of body weight between weeks 36 and 88.
In SURMOUNT-4, patients continuing tirzepatide lost a further 5.5% between weeks 36 and 88.

key_points.point: EMA's PRAC concluded in June 2025 that non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy (NAION) is a very rare side effect of semaglutide (up to 1 in 10,000 users); stop if confirmed.

atoms.fact: EMA's PRAC concluded in June 2025 that non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy (NAION) is a very rare side effect of semaglutide (up to 1 in 10,000 users).
EMA's PRAC advised that semaglutide should be stopped if NAION is confirmed.

key_points.point: Weight loss is smaller in people with type 2 diabetes: semaglutide 2.4 mg gave -9.6% vs -3.4% with placebo at 68 weeks (STEP 2; label Study 3).

atoms.fact: Weight loss with semaglutide 2.4 mg is smaller in people with type 2 diabetes.
In people with type 2 diabetes, semaglutide 2.4 mg gave -9.6% weight change versus -3.4% with placebo at 68 weeks (STEP 2; label Study 3).

key_points.point: Tirzepatide is a dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist, whereas semaglutide acts on the GLP-1 receptor only.

atoms.fact: Tirzepatide is a dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist.
Semaglutide acts on the GLP-1 receptor only.

key_points.point: In the SELECT cardiovascular outcomes trial (label Study 1), semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90), and Wegovy carries this indication.

atoms.fact: In the SELECT cardiovascular outcomes trial (label Study 1), semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90).
Wegovy carries the indication for reducing major adverse cardiovascular events that SELECT supports.

key_points.point: The FDA removed the suicidal behavior and ideation warning from the Wegovy and Zepbound labels in early 2026.

atoms.fact: The FDA removed the suicidal behavior and ideation warning from the Wegovy and Zepbound labels in early 2026.
